attributes.rationale: Data is the primary abstraction, Data Modifiers transform it, and Sequence is a fundamental representation — the three core concepts of the Foundational Abstractions hypothesis.
Schema Provider (language truth), Static Analyser (validation feedback), and Compiler Introspection API (program-specific querying) form the three pillars of the LLM-native toolchain.
Sequence (data representation), emit keyword (Orthon-specific production syntax), and generators/yield (alternative production mechanism) are three approaches to value-over-time semantics.

properties.detail: Concepts enabling adding and composing behaviour across types: mixins, traits with default impls, protocol extensions, and compile-time metaprogramming
Concepts ensuring memory safety at compile time: immutable-by-default, ownership/borrowing, null safety via Option, and lifetime tracking
Concepts for organizing type and declaration boundaries: logical namespaces, nested/inner types, partial class definitions, and singleton declarations

hyperedges.metadata: Compile-time alternatives to reflection: reified generics, derive macros, sealed types, schema code gen
Region-based memory management: arenas, linear ownership, no references, region inference
Concurrency model: STM primitives (Ref, Atom, Agent) and task parallelism

nodes.label: Operator Overloading
nodes.rationale: Overloading of a fixed set of built-in operators via trait implementation, following the Rust model. Uncontroversial and expected for user-defined types.

nodes.label: Derive Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Orthon should provide a general derive/macro mechanism that synthesises structural methods from a type declaration, rather than a dedicated data class keyword. Derive(init, eq, repr, hash) on a type.

nodes.label: Copy-with-Modify
nodes.rationale: A common pattern with data carriers is creating a copy with one or two fields changed. If Orthon has a `with` expression, copy-with-modify is a natural extension.

nodes.label: Structural Equality Derivation
nodes.rationale: Structural equality for data-aggregate types should derive structural comparison of all fields via a derive(eq) mechanism.

nodes.label: Value Semantics by Default
nodes.rationale: All data uses value semantics by default: assignments copy data structurally, equality is structural, and representations are materialized eagerly. Data is compared by its structure, not its identity.

nodes.label: Data Representations
nodes.rationale: Seven representations: Value, Tuple, Reference, Sequence, Set, Option, Result. These are Data Modifier views that combine freely.

nodes.label: Primitive Types
nodes.rationale: Primitive types: Int, Float, Bool, Char, String, Byte, Symbol. Atomic building blocks from which all data is constructed.

nodes.label: Declaration by Assignment
nodes.rationale: A variable is introduced by its first assignment. No separate declaration keyword. Type is inferred from the initializer. Read-before-write is a compile-time error via definite assignment analysis.

nodes.label: Shadowing with Explicit Marker
nodes.rationale: Variable shadowing is permitted but must be syntactically visible via an explicit `let` keyword that signals 'new variable, not reassignment'.

nodes.label: Definite Assignment Analysis
nodes.rationale: The compiler tracks whether a variable has been assigned on all paths before any read. Assigning to an undeclared variable is a compile-time error.

nodes.label: Interface Evolution
nodes.rationale: Interface authors can add new methods with default implementations, reducing the compatibility burden on existing code. Behavioral contracts remain explicit.

nodes.label: Delegate Execution Policy
nodes.rationale: Delegate is an execution policy that wraps a state-owning entity into a delegated execution context. It separates what is executed from how it is executed. Delegate applies to the owner of mutable state, not to arbitrary code.

nodes.label: Execution Closure
nodes.rationale: A delegate = callable + execution policy. The execution policy may include mailbox, scheduler, queue, synchronization, lifetime, cancellation, priorities. Implementation details are not exposed in language semantics.

nodes.label: Property Delegation
nodes.rationale: A property can delegate its getter/setter behavior to a delegate object (lazy, observable, validated, map-backed). Any type implementing a standard Get/Set protocol can be a property delegate.

nodes.label: Unified Toolchain
nodes.rationale: wvy is the single entry point for all operations: init, add, build, run, fmt, lint, test, repl. Zero-config by default, opinionated formatter, curated linter rules. No plugin system.

nodes.label: wvy Tool
nodes.rationale: Single binary, single command, zero configuration package manager, formatter, linter, test runner, and REPL. Source-based package distribution following Go's model.

nodes.label: Single Canonical Language
nodes.rationale: Orthon defines exactly one official syntax. Documentation, compiler diagnostics, formatter output, examples, and generated code always use the canonical keywords. Dialects are lexical-only.

nodes.label: Automatic Differentiation
nodes.rationale: Differentiation is a language construct, not a library. The grad operator correctly handles conditionals, loops, and function calls. Gradients may be computed via runtime tape (default) or source-code transformation.

nodes.label: List[T] — Dynamic Collection
nodes.rationale: Primary ordered collection, dynamically growable, reference semantics. Homogeneous by default via generics; heterogeneous via union types.

nodes.label: Array[T,N] — Fixed Collection
nodes.rationale: Fixed-size collection, value semantics. Stack-allocated for small N. No primitive array syntax — library types with compiler support for literals.

nodes.label: Dynamic Type Escape Hatch
nodes.rationale: Optional dynamic type that disables compile-time member checks and defers them to runtime. Useful for interop, reflection-heavy APIs, and rapid prototyping. Safety boundary: explicit escape hatch, not default.

nodes.label: Emit as Intermediate Result
nodes.rationale: A function may return two kinds of results: intermediate (emit) and final (return). A function becomes Input -> Sequence<Result> -> FinalResult. Emit is a partial result of computation, not a generator.

nodes.label: Named Constants with Auto-Increment
nodes.rationale: Default strategy: named constants with auto-increment (Go-style iota with block syntax). Compiler treats the group as a distinct type for exhaustiveness checking.

nodes.label: Sum Types / Algebraic Data Types
nodes.rationale: Alternative approach: full algebraic enums (Rust/Swift-style) with pattern matching and data per variant. More expressive but more complex.

nodes.label: Value Equality (===)
nodes.rationale: Structural value equality: two values are equal if their data content is structurally equivalent. Recursive field-by-field comparison for compound types. Default comparison for data.

nodes.label: Semantic Equality (==)
nodes.rationale: User-defined equality that may override structural comparison. Custom types can define domain-specific equivalence.

nodes.label: Identity Equality (is)
nodes.rationale: Two references point to the same object in memory. Only meaningful for mutable or reference-counted data.

nodes.label: Result<T,E> Type
nodes.rationale: Monadic error type where T is success type and E is error type. Functions return Result; caller must handle it. ? operator for short-circuit propagation.

nodes.label: Explicit Fallibility
nodes.rationale: Functions that can fail must declare this in their signature. Errors should be visible in the function contract. No unchecked exceptions — all fallibility is declared.

nodes.label: Inferred Error Sets
nodes.rationale: Error Union with inferred, structurally-widening error sets (Zig model). Error tags are unit-like with no payload. Implicit widening of narrower error sets into supersets.

nodes.label: Payload vs Tag-Only Errors
nodes.rationale: Core tension: Result<T,E> (payload-bearing, declared) vs Error Union (tag-only, inferred). May need coexistence as distinct representations for distinct needs.

nodes.label: Exclusive Declarations
nodes.rationale: Three mutually exclusive method declaration keywords: proc (mutating), fun (pure read-only), new (transforming). Each simultaneously declares the method and specifies its effect. No effect matrix.

nodes.label: proc Keyword
nodes.rationale: Mutating operation that changes object state. May return a value (like pop) or nothing. Replaces the mut fun combination from the earlier model.

nodes.label: Execution Program
nodes.rationale: A fully-defined, reproducible, content-addressed representation of everything needed to execute a program. Central abstraction that replaces source code as the primary artifact.

nodes.label: Execution Engines
nodes.rationale: Any consumer that takes an Execution Program: interpreter, REPL, notebook, test runner, debugger, JIT, AOT, OCI builder, MicroVM builder, WASM builder, remote executor.

attributes.summary: Keyword that produces a Sequence value. Three equivalent forms: emit value, return sequence(value), return value ->. Compiler transforms function into resumable state machine.
attributes.rationale: Readable syntax for producing Sequence values, transparently compiled to resumable state machine.

attributes.summary: Values produced over time. Describes what the result is, not how it is produced. One of seven fundamental data representations.
attributes.rationale: Fundamental representation that describes values over time, independent of production mechanism.

attributes.summary: Variables captured by a closure must be explicitly listed or syntactically visible. No silent capture of surrounding scope.
attributes.rationale: Explicitness principle — captured variables must be visible in the function declaration.

attributes.summary: Generic parameters constrained by traits that specify required operations. Associated types and associated constants in traits.
attributes.rationale: Ensures type parameters satisfy behavioural contracts at compile time.

attributes.summary: Type inference everywhere, boundary checking at function signatures, global inference, no separate declaration files, REPL-first dynamic operation.
attributes.rationale: Supports both rapid prototyping (dynamic) and production safety (static) without forcing a permanent choice between them.

attributes.summary: Read-only structured query interface for grammar, type system, and API contracts. LLM Toolchain consumer, not human-written macros.
attributes.rationale: Provides code-queryability benefit of homoiconicity focused on LLM correctness rather than source transformation.

attributes.summary: Memory safety without borrow checker or lifetime annotations. Uses identity-preserved (.) vs identity-changed (!) operations, automatic mutability inference, ownership+escape analysis, move semantics, memory regions.
attributes.rationale: Achieves systems-level memory safety with Python-level syntax complexity, no GC pauses.

attributes.summary: v.method() preserves identity (object unchanged); v!method() changes identity (original not modified). Semantic distinction visible in syntax.
attributes.rationale: Explicit intent via dot and bang operators — you can see whether the object's identity changes at the call site.

attributes.summary: Specific concrete values (strings, numbers, booleans) as their own types. Compose with union types into closed sets. TypeScript-style widening rules.
attributes.rationale: Lightweight closed-set mechanism as alternative to dedicated enum construct. Risk of overlapping with named constants and sum types.

attributes.summary: Central source of truth exposing Grammar Schema, Type System Schema, Standard Library Schema, and Strategy Schema. Versioned, deterministic, strategy-parametric.
attributes.rationale: Single canonical machine-readable truth about the language that an LLM can query at generation time.

attributes.summary: Deep semantic analysis on generated code checking type correctness, policy violations, strategy compatibility, common LLM generation errors.
attributes.rationale: Internal feedback loop for LLMs — catches mistakes before the compiler does, reducing iteration time.

attributes.summary: Queryable runtime interface to compiler's internal knowledge: type queries, autocompletion candidates, trait resolution, scope inspection, diagnostics, symbol docs.
attributes.rationale: Gives LLMs ability to reason about a program without executing it, via stateless deterministic API.
